rows.description:

*🏆 Annie Awards Winner: Best Animated Short Film*

🐻‍❄️ *Learn Art & Animation* https://CreatureArtTeacher.com

*Snow Bear is a hand-drawn animated short film by Oscar-nominated director Aaron Blaise. Featuring over 11,000 traditional drawings, the film blends classic 2D animation with a modern cinematic story.*  Many viewers have described the film as nostalgic—capturing the warmth, craftsmanship, and emotional storytelling of classic hand-drawn animation. That feeling is intentional. Snow Bear was created one drawing at a time in the spirit of the Disney Renaissance era.

*About the Film:*
When a lonely polar bear can't find a friend... he makes one. 

Created with more than *11,000 Drawings* , animated over *3 years* , and crafted entirely by *1 artist* , Oscar-nominated director and Disney veteran _Aaron Blaise_ (_Brother Bear, Mulan, Beauty and the Beast_).

The independent animated film has gone on to win *nearly 40 international awards* to date  including Oscar-qualifying honors.

*🏆 Awards include:*

• Best Animated Short – Santa Fe International Film Festival, Boston Film Festival, Three Rivers
• Audience Choice Awards – Florida Film Festival, Cleveland Film Festival, Nantucket & More!
• Best Family Film – Zagreb Animation Festival, Cordillera
• Planet in Crisis Award - Jackson Wild Film Festival  
• Jury Award for Environmental Impact – SCAD Savannah Film Festival  
• Best International Short – Animation Dingle
• Grand Prize - Toronto Animation Arts Festival Intentional (TAAFI)
• _And many more from festivals worldwide…_

It was also an Official selection in competition at Annecy, Tribeca, San Francisco, Chicago and many more. We are so happy to share it with all of you! 
------------------------------------------------------------

*ABOUT THE FILM*  
_Snow Bear_ is a hand-drawn story about empathy, nature, family, and the rapidly changing Arctic.

rows.title: How to Make Hand-Drawn Animation | Straight-Ahead and Keyframing
rows.description:
Learn how to make hand-drawn animation from start to finish. In this tutorial, animator Kohana Wilson (they/them) walks through the tools, techniques, and principles behind classic paper animation, from your very first drawn frame to a finished animated sequence in After Effects. Whether you're animating an abstract dot, a dragonfly, or a cartwheeling character, this video breaks down the full traditional animation workflow — from rough sketches to a polished, moving sequence.

You'll learn:
- The science behind animation — persistence of vision, explained with a zoetrope, praxinoscope, and flip book
- Essential tools: light boxes, peg bars, and paper choices for hand-drawn animation
- Straight-ahead animation — drawing frame by frame in sequence
- Keyframe animation and in-betweening — planning key poses first, then filling in the motion
- Core animation principles: squash and stretch, easing in and out, follow-through, overlapping action, and smear frames
- How to clean up rough animation and scan your frames for digital editing
- Bringing your sequence to life in Adobe After Effects

Artwork references included: Lotte Reiniger, John Canemaker, Winsor McCay, David Ehrlich, Eadweard J. Muybridge, Mary Beams, Maria Lassnig, and William Kentridge.

rows.title: Making 3D animation look painterly (it's easier than you think)
rows.description:
In this video, I'll go over a surprisingly simple way to make your stylized 3D renders feel like a painting. I do it by painting over Object Space Normal Maps, which is not as scary as it sounds. This technique allows us to capture the feeling of a 2D painting while maintaining the flexibility of 3D. 

I used Blender, Substance Painter, Substance Designer, and Rebelle to make the stylized tea kettle scene. 

Thanks for watching :)

Instagram: instagram.com/codygindy/
TikTok: tiktok.com/@codygindy

Chapters:

0:00 Intro
0:18 Top Five Favorite Things (about this technique)
2:19 Prerequisites
2:50 3 Basic Steps
3:05 Demo
4:30 Why does this work?
5:30 How Normals Work
6:39 Base color?
7:27 Conversions


Frequently Asked Questions

How do you paint World Space in Substance Painter/How do you paint on two channels at the same time?

In this video, I'm painting on a custom channel. The only reason it's "world" is because that's what I named it. Substance has no idea what it actually is and you can't preview it as a normal map in the software. You'll have to export it to your renderer to test it. 

Tyson explains the setup in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=snJXgLqXhb4


How do you convert your painted object space map to tangent space?

You can just bake it again to a new image texture, but this time in tangent space. Just make sure your painterly object space normal map is plugged into your shader when you do it. 


Can I do this procedurally or semi-procedurally?

Yeah! Check out these videos:

Painterly shader with nodes: https://youtu.be/AtetvOEcZt8?si=dNj-8toj3XQxE4aO&t=890

Brush strokes with geometry nodes: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MgZsVBVZ3Nc&t=9s

Snapping normals (this one's in Korean, but is still pretty easy to follow from just the visuals): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_wxvwwYWZHs&t=141s



Can I paint the normal map in Blender?

Yes! Check out these videos:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WyxPN2HRaFk
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IoIwVWmdqL4

Both Rig setups delivered solid results, but Blender did a better job with the mesh bending parts.

Plus, Blender offers advanced rigging tools you'd typically find in premium software like Spine 2D or Moho…except it’s free (with a few extra steps, of course)

rows.title: Why Does Twitter HATE This Indie Show? Zipped Up
rows.description:
Recently a new clip was posted for an upcoming indie pilot, but it got alot of backlash online. So why do people hate zipped up? Lets talk about it. 

So zipped up is an upcoming indie animated pilot by bliptoons studio. It had a successful kickstarter campaign, raising over 23 thousand dollars. 

The other day they put up this clip from the song Big Top Big Shots in the pilot, i’ll roll a clip. 

Almost immediately this post got alot of pushback and criticism. 

The main complaints pointing out that the art style looks like it’s vivziepops, people thinking it was made by viv or just saying they’re fatigued on that art style, they’re sick of it. 

There’s other critiques too like the character Dom being the stereotypical tv head archetype, or kester looking like tadc mixed with helluva boss. 

Some of the team members who worked on the show responded and were quite sad about the backlash. 

One asking people to be kinder when it properly comes out

The creator of the show min put up a couple tweets, pointing out that indie projects have been getting alot of hate in recent months. They thanked the people giving constructive criticism though. 

So I have a couple thoughts about this. 

So the reason the show looks like its vivziepops is because if we go to the studio that is making the pilot, their employees worked at spindlehorse, glitch, zamination and others. They’re also working on the amazing digital fight club. 

It reminds me of the early 2000’s where artists would work on cartoons, and then later on make their own shows that blew up. It’s normal to be inspired by things that came before you or that you worked on. 

Lastly I think the indie animation genre has definitely aged and shifted demographics. Like in 2019 you could do whatever and get praise because there was no competition. But now expectations are super high, like people will compare your stuff to hazbin hotel or tadc which isn’t entirely fair, those two shows were lightning in a bottle.

So what do you think? Have you heard of zipped up? Let me know down below. 

#zippedup #indieanimation #indieseries

rows.title: ULTIMATE Indie Animation Tier List… 🔥 #shorts
This New Indie Animation Surprised Me! Wastelandia Pilot Review
rows.description:
Today the latest indie animated pilot called wastelandia released. Is it any good? Let’s talk about it. 

Wastelandia is a 6 minute pilot created by youtuber Izzzyzzz. It’s a slice of life comedy which follows Zoe,  Alice, and Moth as they navigate their early twenties and all the weirdness that comes with becoming an adult. 

First up the animation and art style is wonderful, easily one of the best looking indie pilots on youtube so far. I love how the colour palettes swap based on the area. The house is full of warm colours while moth’s work is dark and moody. 

The voice acting is great and each character feels unique.

There’s also plenty of fun references and attention to detail in the backgrounds. 

There are a few issues though. 

First up the audio balancing is a little off. Some of the sound effects are way too loud and overlay on top of the voice lines, making it hard to follow. 

The pacing is extremely fast, if it was slower we would get more attached to the characters. 

And lastly the writing is a bit hit or miss. Some of the jokes i didn’t really find funny, like the reddit ones. 

What do you think? Have you watched wastelandia yet? Let me know down below. 

Check the pilot out here:

This brand-spanking-new installment of the Autodale series follows the lives of the Robinson family; Autodale's perfect citizens.

I've wanted to make an animated short film based around the life-cycle of an Autodale citizen/family for a very long time. We've only ever seen Autodale through the eyes of children. All of the other short films in the series focus on skeptical children being successfully brainwashed/indoctrinated into complacency with Autodale's dystopian ways.
